title: The 2024 State of Tech Talent Report
reason: Web survey of 418 valid records (Dec 2023 to Feb 2024); onboarding averages 4.8 months to normal productivity, though secondary sites cite 321 organizations.

title: Coping with the Sudden Loss of an Indispensable Employee: An Exploratory Case Study
reason: Peer-reviewed case study of a small manufacturer tracking knowledge flows to the replacement with real-time surveys and interviews; one firm, no headcount figures.

title: An analysis of the new job openings and labor turnover data by size of firm
reason: Official BLS method article on JOLTS turnover by firm size; gives context for small-firm turnover data but no onboarding or knowledge-loss figures.

title: Create an Exceptional Onboarding Journey for Your New Employees
reason: Gallup onboarding guidance from its 2019 perspective paper; names no survey sample, so use only as qualitative support.

title: Unlocking the Power of Onboarding to Aid Employee Retention
reason: Cites Brandon Hall's onboarding study: 41% of organizations see over 5% new-hire turnover; the article does not state the sample size.

title: There Are Significant Business Costs to Replacing Employees
reason: Review of 30 turnover-cost case studies, with a median cost near 20% of salary for lower-paid roles; the page returned 403 to WebFetch, so verify before citing.

title: Labor Market Fact Sheet (rev. May 2022)
publisher: U.S. Small Business Administration, Office of Advocacy
reason: Government fact sheet using JOLTS data on small-establishment job openings; context on small-business hiring, not on knowledge loss; WebFetch returned 403.

title: Measuring the impact of knowledge loss: a longitudinal study
reason: Longitudinal case study of an Australian government department linking knowledge loss to longer time to competence; the repository returned 403, so verify the figures.

title: Express Employment Professionals release on knowledge transfer when older workers retire
reason: Staffing-firm-commissioned Harris Poll survey where 84% of US employees call unpassed knowledge a big loss; vendor-sourced, and the page returned a 500 error.
